tolerances.function: sklearn.preprocessing.StandardScaler().fit(X, sample_weight=...): mean_, var_ and scale_; and its transform
tolerances.rule: mean_, var_ and scale_: relative 1e-12 of reference values computed with math.fsum (over the rounded products w*x for mean_, and over w*(x - mean)**2 for var_); test_preprocessing's weighted-tolerance row checks mean_ and var_ on one fit of 1000 random weighted samples (scale_ is the square root of var_). The transform, (x - mean_) / scale_, carries mean_'s error as an absolute error of about a few ulp(mean_) / scale_, so near mean_ its relative error can be anything (a constant column gives -0x1p-50 here against scikit-learn's -0x1p-48). The small weighted rows (fit, transform, partial_fit, NaNs) match scikit-learn to the bit
tolerances.reason: the weighted sums are np.matmul(sample_weight, X), as in scikit-learn's _incremental_mean_and_var, and Sagebrush's matmul doesn't reproduce OpenBLAS's summation order (ruled: results through np.dot or @ may differ from scikit-learn by a few ulps; everything else is bit-exact). Weighted partial_fit goes through the same sums, so it can differ by a few ulps too; the row doesn't bound it
